On `2023-05-18` GATK obtained a large VCF with SNP calls among all the ddRAD
samples. The VCF is a very incomplete matrix of genotypes. We need describe
the missingness in that matrix. How many SNPs are genotyped in at least *n*
samples? What samples have less than a certain fraction of SNPs genotyped?
We use `vcftools` to answer these questions.

# Individual Filtering Options 

There may be some individuals with low data. Before deciding what individuals
to remove from the data set (i) we need to see the proportion of sites per individual,
and (ii) we need to see the proportion of data they miss.

The `--missing-indv` option commands `vcftools` to  generate a file reporting
the missingness on a per-individual basis. The file has the suffix ".imiss".

```{bash}
VCF=../2023-05-18/crepi.vcf
if [ ! -e crepi.imiss ]; then
   vcftools --vcf $VCF \
            --out crepi \
            --missing-indv 1> vcftools.log 2> vcftools.err
fi
```

We graphically represent the results, and draw a threshold to determine the filter of the individuals.

```{r}
missingness <- read.table('crepi.imiss', header = TRUE)
plot(ecdf(missingness$F_MISS),
     xlab = 'Fraction of sites missing',
     main = 'ECDF of fraction of sites missing per individual')
abline(v = 0.95, col = 'red', lty = 2)
VeryBad <- as.character(missingness[missingness$F_MISS > 0.95, 'INDV'])
VeryBad
write.table(VeryBad, file = 'VeryBad.txt', quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
```

Given the discontinuity in the distribution of missingness, it seems reasonable to
draw a threshold at 95% of missing data. Out of 96 individuals, 90 are left.

```{bash}
VCF=../2023-05-18/crepi.vcf
if [ ! -e crepi_indv.recode.vcf ]; then
   vcftools --vcf $VCF \
            --out crepi_indv \
            --remove VeryBad.txt \
            --recode \
            --recode-INFO-all 1>> vcftools.log 2>> vcftools.err
fi
```

# Sites Missing and Filtering 
After having removed the individuals with very low amounts of data, we can check
the missingness by sites, and filter sites. We start from over 7 million sites, and
it is not surprising that most of them are not genotyped in a large portion of samples.

## Missing Sites
```{bash}
if [ ! -e crepi.lmiss ]; then
   vcftools --vcf crepi_indv.recode.vcf \
            --out crepi \
            --missing-site 1>> vcftools.log 2>> vcftools.err
fi
```

```{r}
missingsite <- read.table('crepi.lmiss', header = TRUE)
plot(ecdf(missingsite$N_MISS/2),
     xlab = 'Number of genotypes missing per site',
     main = 'ECDF of number of sites missing')

plot(0:40, dim(missingsite)[1] * ecdf(missingsite$N_MISS/2)(0:40), pch = 19,
     ylab = 'Number of sites left', xlab = 'Allowed number of missing individuals out of 90')
```

I note that `vcftools` reports and filters missing chromosomes, not *genotypes*, and
that's why I divide by 2 above, to keep count of (diploid) individuals, instead of
their chromosomes. Allowing no more than 30 genotypes missing in a site retrieves more
han 50000 sites, which is good enough. We could use the filter `--max-missing-count 60`
(because, again, `vcftools` counts chromosomes!) or `--max-missing 0.667`, because the
name of this parameter is misleading and it actually means the minimum fraction of
genotypes (or chromosomes) with data. We also apply the following filtering options
to generate a cleaner data set

#### Position filtering
`--thin` Specified distance between one site and the next.

#### Variant type Filtering
`--remove-indels` Exclude sites that contain an idel (any variant that alters the lenght of the REF allele).

#### Info Field Filtering
`--mac` Include only sites with Minor Allele Count higher or equal to <value>
`--max-allels` Include only sites with a number of alleles lower or equal to <value>

#### Genotype Value Filtering
`--max-meanDP` Includes only sites with mean depth values (over all included individuals) lower or equal to the <value>. These options require that the "DP" FORMAT tag is included for each site.
`--minGQ` Exclude all genotypes with a quality below the threshold specified. This option requires that the "GQ" FORMAT tag is specified for all sites.

#### VCF Output Options
`--recode` Generate a new .vcf file from the input after applying the filtering options specified.
`--recode-INFO-all` Keep the INFO key present in the input file.

```{bash}
if [ ! -e summary_distances.txt ]; then
   gawk 'BEGIN{
      CURRENTCHROM = ""
      LASTPOS = 0
   }(/^[^#]/){
      if (($1 == CURRENTCHROM) && (LASTPOS > 0)){
         F[$2 - LASTPOS]++
         LASTPOS = $2
      } else {
         CURRENTCHROM = $1
         LASTPOS = $2
      }
   }END{
      for (f in F) print f "\t" F[f]
   }' crepi_indv.recode.vcf | \
   sort -nk 1,1 > summary_distances.txt
fi
```

```{r}
distances <- read.table('summary_distances.txt',
                        col.names = c('D', 'Freq'))
plot(distances$D, distances$Freq, log = 'xy')
abline(v = 200, col = 'red', lty = 2)
```

```{bash}
if [ ! -e crepi_sites.recode.vcf ]; then
   vcftools --vcf crepi_indv.recode.vcf \
            --out crepi_sites \
            --thin 200 \
            --max-missing 0.667 \
            --remove-indels \
            --mac 2 \
            --max-meanDP 1000 \
            --recode --recode-INFO-all 1>> vcftools.log 2>> vcftools.err
fi
```

The `--thin 200` filter actually removes a lot of data, without being specially strict.
Many pairs of SNPs will still be in linkage disequilibrium.
This prevents us from using the VCF in any meaningful subsequent analysis. But it conveys
some information about the nature of variation within our samples. Definitely, SNPs are much
more tightly clustered than if randomly distributed among contigs. This is in part a consequence
of discovering SNPs only close to restriction enzyme cutting sites. Without the information of
read positions, we cannot evaluate if the number of SNPs per locus is well distributed or not.
But the distances gathered above tell us that 60% of adjacent SNP pairs are less than
10 bases apart.
